problem: Real-time spatial audio generation struggles with the tradeoff between quality and inference latency, and struggles to capture precise spatial information from multimodal inputs.
approach: SwanSphere proposes a causal autoregressive diffusion transformer with a Spatial Video–Audio Contrastive learning strategy and multi-objective online direct preference optimization to align video and audio domains for streaming spatial audio generation.
contribution: Achieves superior performance in both video-to-spatial and text-to-spatial audio generation tasks with an automated annotation pipeline for spatial captions.

problem: Most time-series forecasters use backpropagation-based training which increases computational cost and limits structural transparency of predictions.
approach: FIPN grows its architecture layer-by-layer through candidate generation and validation-based selection without backpropagation, coupling fuzzy rule antecedents with Fourier-enhanced polynomial consequents to capture periodic structures.
contribution: Achieves competitive accuracy with compact model size and provides rule- and structure-level explanations for long-horizon forecasting.

problem: Speculative inference accelerates LLMs but existing safety defenses are incompatible with it, providing no inherent safety guarantees.
approach: SafeSpec integrates risk estimation directly into the verification process with a lightweight latent safety head, applying rollback and safety-guided reflective multi-sampling when unsafe generations are detected.
contribution: Reduces attack success rates by 15% while preserving 2.06× inference speedup on Qwen3-32B, demonstrating joint optimization of safety and efficiency.

problem: The reversal curse exposes asymmetry in autoregressive models where inverse relations are not accessible even when forward relations are learned.
approach: Chiral Transformer introduces an involutive adjoint mapping operator through contrastive regularization, using Adjoint-Induced Retrieval as a structured readout of entity representations rather than autoregressive generation.
contribution: Reaches 65.07% accuracy on Fact-Inv-300, substantially improving inverse factual access by treating the reversal curse as a representation-access problem.

problem: Multi-device transformer inference requires high inter-device bandwidth, making it impractical for bandwidth-constrained environments.
approach: ASTRA integrates sequence parallelism with mixed-precision attention using vector-quantized codes for non-local embeddings while keeping local attention full precision, introducing Noise-Augmented Quantization and Distributed Class Tokens.
contribution: Achieves up to 2.64× speedup and 15.25× over prior baselines while operating at bandwidths as low as 10 Mbps.

problem: Discrete flow matching sampling methods like τ-leaping do not efficiently handle limited function evaluations.
approach: TR-CIE sampler uses schedule-based time reparameterization to rescale the time grid and cumulative-intensity extrapolation to improve approximation of stepwise cumulative intensities.
contribution: Improves sampling quality under limited function evaluations without additional model evaluations on text generation and text-to-image benchmarks.

problem: Multi-agent imitation learning lacks theoretical analysis in linear Markov games with function approximation.
approach: Proposes leveraging linear structure to replace state-action concentrability coefficients with feature-level concentrability, and provides a computationally efficient interactive MAIL algorithm.
contribution: Achieves sample complexity depending only on feature dimension d and outperforms behavioral cloning on Tic-Tac-Toe and Connect4.

problem: While Transformers can be simulated in RASP languages, it remains unclear whether trained models actually implement simple interpretable programs.
approach: Proposes a method to extract RASP programs from trained Transformers by faithfully re-parameterizing as RASP and applying causal interventions to discover small sufficient sub-programs.
contribution: Recovers simple and interpretable RASP programs from length-generalizing transformers on algorithmic and formal language tasks.

problem: Implicit feedback-based collaborative models face privacy concerns when distributed across multiple parties, and differential privacy causes utility degradation.
approach: DPIMF uses objective perturbation with redesigned loss function and importance sampling to reduce noise scale required for privacy preservation in cross-silo recommendation.
contribution: Achieves better privacy-utility trade-off than state-of-the-art methods on benchmark datasets while maintaining formal privacy guarantees.

problem: Root cause analysis for rare events in structural equation models lacks a formal definition of causal pathways and testable implications.
approach: Proposes formal definition of causal pathways for rare events and identifies conditions where implications depend only on causal abstraction of the pathway.
contribution: Bridges verbal causal explanations and detailed causal modeling through abstraction to pathways of rare events.

problem: RL rollout phase is an efficiency bottleneck due to long-tail bubbles across data parallel ranks, especially in long-context scenarios.
approach: BubbleSpec exploits idle time windows of faster ranks to pre-generate rollout results serving as drafts for speculative decoding while maintaining strict synchronous property.
contribution: Reduces decoding steps by ~50% and increases rollout throughput by up to 1.8× without compromising algorithm exactness.

problem: Fixed goal representations in self-supervised goal-conditioned RL are either too concrete or too abstract depending on observation structure.
approach: Proposes construction of hierarchical latent goal spaces using energy functions to learn subset relations between observations.
contribution: Agents achieve higher task success and greater generalization to novel tasks compared to agents using purely observational goals.

problem: Fixed intervention directions and strengths in representation-based LLM alignment cause degradation of general capabilities on benign inputs.
approach: MARI introduces multi-adapter mechanism with competitive experts capturing non-linear correction patterns and energy-based gating for adaptive intervention.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art alignment on TruthfulQA and safety benchmarks while maintaining general capabilities on MMLU and ARC.

problem: Current LLM evaluation benchmarks bifurcate into static code generation or text-only reasoning, missing the synthesis needed for interactive scientific demonstrations.
approach: InteractScience proposes a hybrid framework integrating programmatic functional testing with visually-grounded qualitative assessment across five scientific disciplines.
contribution: First benchmark dedicated to interactive scientific application generation reveals critical gaps in grounding scientific reasoning within interactive interfaces.

problem: Real-world RL agents face unobservable and time-varying delays when interacting with environments, which standard MDPs do not model.
approach: Introduces interaction layer framework enabling agents to generate matrices of possible future actions anticipating delay horizons, with Actor-Critic with Delay Adaptation algorithm.
contribution: Significantly outperforms state-of-the-art approaches across locomotion benchmarks including real-world measured delays.

problem: Scientific problems are underdetermined with multiple equally-consistent hypotheses, requiring not only valid explanations but systematic exploration of hypothesis sets.
approach: HypoSpace treats LLMs as samplers over finite hypothesis spaces and evaluates on Validity, Uniqueness, and Recovery across deterministic structured domains.
contribution: Reveals capability-dependent coverage failure: models maintain validity while exhibiting reduced uniqueness and recovery as hypothesis spaces become larger.

problem: Search-augmented LLMs remain insufficient for addressing diverse user needs without recognizing query intent across users and preferred response forms.
approach: BESPOKE collects authentic chat and search histories from humans and pairs responses with fine-grained preference scores and diagnostic feedback.
contribution: First realistic benchmark for personalization in search-augmented LLMs reveals key requirements for effective personalization in information-seeking tasks.

problem: Discrete diffusion language models cannot use autoregressive test-time scaling methods due to parallel decoding over entire sequences.
approach: LLaDA-S performs Hierarchical Trajectory Search with dynamic pruning, uses Self-Verified Feedback from intermediate completions, and introduces local branching with partial remasking.
contribution: Matches best-of-N performance with substantially fewer function evaluations across four reasoning and code generation benchmarks.

problem: Code generation formulated as strictly monotonic token appending misses the interleaved forward generation and revision inherent in programming.
approach: Stream of Revision introduces action tokens enabling models to backtrack and edit history within a single forward pass, internalizing revision without external tools.
contribution: Significantly reduces vulnerabilities in secure code generation with minimal inference overhead.

problem: SVG animation generation requires bridging discrete code representations with continuous visual dynamics while preserving structural editability.
approach: VAnim reconceptualizes animation as Sparse State Updates on persistent SVG DOM trees with Identification-First Motion Planning and Rendering-Aware Reinforcement Learning.
contribution: First LLM-based framework for text-to-SVG animation compresses sequence length by 9.8× while guaranteeing topological isomorphism.

problem: Compositional two-sample tests often require log-transformations and only detect mean differences, lacking generality for non-Euclidean data.
approach: Proposes studentized energy statistic constructed from spherical harmonics theory without log-based methods, incorporating U-statistics and studentization.
contribution: Establishes asymptotic normality for spherical harmonics based test statistics, avoiding need for permutation tests.

problem: High-dimensional Ising model estimation with limited target samples struggles to effectively use auxiliary datasets of unknown relevance.
approach: Trans-Ising combines loss-based source screening with two-stage estimation using held-out target pseudolikelihood followed by folded-concave penalty.
contribution: Achieves lower estimation errors than target-only and naive pooling with exact graph selection consistency.

problem: Low-rank RNNs lack independence interpretations for assigning distinct computational roles to different latent dimensions.
approach: FacRNN reformulates lrRNN under VAE framework with group-wise independence assumptions and partial correlation penalty encouraging independence.
contribution: Consistently improves disentanglement and interpretability of neural latent trajectories on monkey M1 and mouse imaging data.

problem: The role of attention sinks in diffusion transformers remains unclear compared to their assumed importance in autoregressive models.
approach: Presents causal analysis dynamically identifying dominant attention recipients per timestep and suppressing them via interventions on score and value paths.
contribution: Removing attention sinks does not degrade text-image alignment on Stable Diffusion 3, only under stronger interventions showing metric-dependent boundaries.

problem: Diffusion language models using bidirectional attention break standard prefix KV caching, failing to translate parallelism into speed gains.
approach: WeDLM uses Topological Reordering to move observed tokens to physical prefix while preserving logical positions with causal attention and streaming decoding.
contribution: Delivers speedups approaching 3× on reasoning benchmarks and up to 10× in low-entropy generation while preserving quality.

problem: Point-cloud registration often requires correspondence computation and struggles with poor initial alignment and partial overlap.
approach: MMD-Reg proposes correspondence-free registration using Maximum Mean Discrepancy approximated with random Fourier features, solved with Levenberg-Marquardt.
contribution: Achieves differentiability and linear complexity while supporting challenging conditions and integration with neural models.

problem: Visual token reduction for multimodal LLMs overlooks positional and attentional consistency, resulting in distorted representations.
approach: RESTORE calibrates token reduction by augmenting attention weights based on relative distances and introduces distinctive anchor selection for token merging.
contribution: Consistently improves accuracy of various reduction methods while maintaining computational efficiency.

problem: Particle filtering for inference-time scaling is vulnerable to overconfident process reward models causing premature exploitation and particle impoverishment.
approach: Entropic Particle Filtering monitors search diversity via entropy and introduces Look-ahead Modulation to evaluate state potential based on successors.
contribution: Significantly outperforms strong baselines achieving up to 50% relative improvement on challenging math benchmarks.

problem: Lifelong person re-identification assumes stable appearance but real identities reappear with substantial clothing changes causing representation drift.
approach: Framework disentangles identity-intrinsic representations from clothing-induced biases with Dynamic Identity-Anchor Alignment for stage-wise distribution shifts.
contribution: Demonstrates superior performance and representational stability on LTCC and PRCC benchmarks across multiple learning stages.

problem: Existing evolutionary model merging overlooks the underlying performance landscape of coefficient space in favor of hand-crafted operators.
approach: EvoGM employs learnable generative modeling with dual-generator architecture and cycle-consistent learning to adaptively sample merging candidates.
contribution: Significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines exhibiting robust performance on both seen and unseen tasks.

problem: Training-data influence estimators aggregate influence over all loop iterations, obscuring when examples matter in looped transformer computation.
approach: Step-Decomposed Influence decomposes TracIn into influence trajectories by unrolling recurrent computation graph with TensorSketch for scalability.
contribution: Scales excellently at transformer scale with per-step insights into latent reasoning process.

problem: Distribution matching distillation reduces sample diversity in few-step image generation, requiring perceptual or adversarial regularization for stability.
approach: DP-DMD uses role-separated distillation with teacher-derived target-prediction objective for early steps to preserve diversity and standard DMD for later steps.
contribution: Preserves sample diversity while maintaining competitive visual quality without perceptual or adversarial regularization.

problem: Existing neural combinatorial optimization for MILPs relies heavily on labeled data and struggles with feasibility and mixed-type variable modeling.
approach: Proposes unsupervised Langevin sampler learning only integer variables while solving continuous variables via exact LP solver with unified energy function.
contribution: Achieves 100% feasibility without post-processing and matches or outperforms supervised solvers on benchmarks.

problem: LLMs suffer from representation collapse in long-context settings due to pathological extremes of homogenization and isolation.
approach: TRSP employs Triangular Box mechanism scaled by length-aware gate to regularize token interaction topology while preserving effective rank.
contribution: On NoLiMa at 8× training length retains 83% accuracy and surpasses Differential Transformer and Gated Attention by approximately 30-50 points.

problem: InfoNCE training with in-batch negatives depends on hard negatives but explicit mining is costly or heuristic-driven.
approach: HOBIT solves optimization problem to yield mini-batches where each query is exposed to hard yet informative negative examples using greedy algorithm.
contribution: Incurs negligible overhead while significantly outperforming state-of-the-art batching methods with O(1-1/e) approximation guarantee.

problem: Fair regression methods rely on squared error loss making them fragile under heavy-tailed noise.
approach: Proposes general framework for robust regression under demographic parity applying to M-estimators with optimal fair transformation and interpolation scheme.
contribution: Shows clear improvements over existing fair regression in both robustness and predictive performance across simulations and real data.

problem: LLMs waste substantial compute by producing long, incorrect responses when using chain-of-thought reasoning.
approach: Formalizes dynamic abstention as explicit RL action within regularized framework where abstention at low value function outperforms baselines.
contribution: Derives principled and efficient value function approximation with improved selective accuracy on mathematical reasoning tasks.

problem: Existing guardrails perform post-hoc detection risking unsafe content exposure before detection, with latency constraints limiting accuracy.
approach: PlugGuard enables streaming risk detection via Streaming Latent Dynamics Head modeling temporal evolution of risk with Anchored Temporal Consistency loss.
contribution: Achieves 22.80% F1 score gain over state-of-the-art streaming guardrails while using 20M parameters and adding <0.5ms per-token latency.

problem: Real-world multivariate time series have diverse inter-channel correlations and temporal causality constraints not addressed by MLP-based mixers.
approach: Proposes cluster-aware causal mixer grouping channels by correlations with dedicated embeddings and sequential anomaly-scoring accumulating evidence over time.
contribution: Consistently achieves superior performance across six public benchmarks for online multivariate time-series anomaly detection.

problem: Vision-Language-Action models show spurious invariance to semantic changes and extreme brittleness to environmental perturbations despite high benchmark scores.
approach: LIBERO-Gen designs hierarchical diagnostic protocol spanning In-distribution, Compositional, and Domain Generalization shifts with explicit distributional assumptions.
contribution: Reveals performance stratifications previously masked by standard metrics identifying perceptual instability and action binding as primary failure modes.
